items.item_text: Education/Training: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in education, business administration, public administration, workforce development, or a related field. A master’s degree in business, education, or public administration is preferred.

The following describes the education, experience, knowledge, skills and abilities required to enter the job and/or be learned within a short period of time in order to successfully perform the assigned duties.
Education and Experience Guidelines :

Experience: Two years of progressively responsible experience in program management, workforce development, or regional collaboration, including project oversight and reporting responsibilities, and one year of supervisory or lead experience. Experience with California Community College workforce programs (e.g., Strong Workforce, Perkins, CAEP, CAI, or K–16), managing multi-institutional partnerships or grant-funded projects, and developing or using data systems for program evaluation and reporting is desirable.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
Principles of program management, program planning, and evaluation.
Lead and coordinate multiple regional initiatives simultaneously.
California Community College system and regional workforce development structures.
Apply an equity-minded framework and ensure programs, services, and processes are designed and delivered to meet the varying needs of all students and partners.
Labor market analysis and performance metrics related to student outcomes.
Plan and organize work to meet changing priorities and deadlines.
Fiscal management and reporting requirements for public grants and contracts.
Coordinate collaboration and facilitate productive working relationships across diverse institutions and stakeholders.
Data collection, analysis, and visualization methods.
Interpret and apply federal, state, and district policies related to workforce and grant programs.
Principles of supervision, training, and performance evaluation.
Analyze data, prepare reports, and present findings to varied audiences.
Modern office practices, cloud-based collaboration tools, and project management software.
Supervise, motivate, train, and evaluate assigned staff.
Pertinent federal, state, and local laws, codes, and regulations related to workforce and grant programs.
Exercise initiative, independent judgment, and diplomacy in a complex regional environment.
Current and emerging workforce development practices, initiatives, trends, and industry needs.
Demonstrate awareness and appreciation of the cultural diversity of the community.

Methods to successfully support individuals with varying backgrounds, which includes persons with disabilities, various gender identities, sexual orientation, individuals from historically underrepresented communities and other groups.
Work effectively in a hybrid environment with occasional travel throughout the region.
Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing.
Interact and work effectively with a diverse population utilizing exceptional interpersonal and intercultural skills.

Exercise sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, faculty, and staff.
Operate office equipment including computers and supportive software.
